FACT_ID: sec14-R01 | anchor: A01
Solo drivers just carry papers, while permit drivers also carry a twenty-one-plus coach, eighteen-plus for kin [A01].
Why it matters: group carry-coach; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec14-F01, sec14-F02 [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec14-R02 | anchor: A01
Nineteen-plus applicants wait sixty days or graduate driver-ed, while their coaches qualify at twenty-one or eighteen for family [A01].
Why it matters: group wait-coach; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec14-F03, sec14-F02 [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec14-R03 | anchor: FXsec14R03
A conviction for driving after illegally drinking alcohol, with a blood-alcohol level of point zero eight percent or more, may bring the same penalties faced by adults. Providing or selling alcohol to someone under twenty-one exposes the provider to a fine, license suspension and jail [FXsec14R03].
Why it matters: group drink-supply; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec14-F04, sec14-F05 [FXsec14R03].
Source: [FXsec14R03 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec14-R04 | anchor: FXsec14R04
Supplying or selling alcohol to someone under twenty-one exposes you to a fine up to twenty-five hundred dollars, mandatory license suspension for up to one year, and twelve months in jail. An under-twenty-one person using or trying to use a fake identification to drink or buy alcohol faces at least five hundred dollars in fines, at least fifty service hours, up to twelve months in jail, and mandatory suspension lasting six months to one year [FXsec14R04].
Why it matters: group penalty-duo; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec14-F05, sec14-F06 [FXsec14R04].
Source: [FXsec14R04 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec14-R05 | anchor: A02
Regular licenses cap at twenty-six thousand pounds outside CDL land, while CDLs open rigs, buses, tankers, big school buses, and hazmat [A02].
Why it matters: group license-split; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec14-F07, sec14-F08 [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec14-R06 | anchor: A02
Fifteen-rider buses need only an endorsement stamped with the cap, while sixteen-plus buses demand the full CDL [A02].
Why it matters: group bus-split; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec14-F09, sec14-F08 [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec14-R07 | anchor: A02
Genuine AAA permits translate for travel and license nothing, while store-bought versions license nothing legally and their sale is a Class 1 crime [A02].
Why it matters: group permit-truth; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec14-F10, sec14-F11 [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec14-R08 | anchor: FXsec14R08
Local AAA branches issue international permits except to people with suspended or revoked driving privileges. A visitor using a home-country license should carry a translation with it [FXsec14R08].
Why it matters: group travel-papers; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec14-F10 [FXsec14R08].
Source: [FXsec14R08 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0034]
